title: A skyscraper sheaf of sets at a point is the direct image of the constant sheaf on the closure of the point
statement:
Let $Y$ be a topological space, $y\in Y$, $W=\overline{\{y\}}$ the closure of $\{y\}$ with inclusion $i_W:W	o Y$, and $A$ a set. Let $i_{y,*}A$ be the skyscraper sheaf at $y$ with value $A$: the sheaf of sets on $Y$ with $(i_{y,*}A)(V)=A$ if $y\in V$ and $(i_{y,*}A)(V)=\{*\}$ (a one-point set) if $y
otin V$ ($V\subseteq Y$ open), the restriction maps being the identity of $A$ when the smaller open contains $y$ and the map to $\{*\}$ otherwise. Let $(i_W)_*\underline A_W$ be the sheaf of sets $V\mapsto\{$locally constant maps $V\cap W	o A\}$ on $Y$ (restriction of maps as restriction maps). Then: (1) for every open $V\subseteq Y$, $V\cap W
eq\emptyset$ if and only if $y\in V$; (2) if $y\in V$, every locally constant map $V\cap W	o A$ is constant; (3) consequently the maps $\kappa_V:(i_{y,*}A)(V)	o(i_W)_*\underline A_W(V)$, sending $a\in A$ to the constant map with value $a$ when $y\in V$, and $*$ to the empty map when $y
otin V$, are bijective and form an isomorphism of sheaves of sets $\kappa:i_{y,*}A\xrightarrow{\sim}(i_W)_*\underline A_W$.

Skyscraper sheaf as in Sheaves, Definition Tag 009A (label definition-skyscraper-sheaf, sheaves.tex line 3273); its stalks are described in Sheaves, Lemma Tag 009B (label lemma-skyscraper-stalks).

proof.text: *Step 1 (claim (1)).* Let $V\subseteq Y$ be open. If $y\in V$, then $y\in V\cap W$ since $y\in\overline{\{y\}}=W$, so $V\cap W\neq\emptyset$. Conversely let $w\in V\cap W$. Since $w$ lies in the closure of $\{y\}$, every open neighbourhood of $w$ meets $\{y\}$ (a point not in the closure of a set has an open neighbourhood disjoint from it, namely the complement of the closure); $V$ is an open neighbourhood of $w$, so $V\cap\{y\}\neq\emptyset$, i.e. $y\in V$.

source.place: Modules, proof of Lemma Tag 0CAL (label lemma-constructible-in-constant, line 3133), the omitted claim 'i_{x,*}F_x is a constant sheaf on the closure of x'; written out by the agent

proof.text: *Step 2 (claim (2)).* Let $V\subseteq Y$ be open with $y\in V$, so $y\in V\cap W$, and let $g:V\cap W\to A$ be locally constant (every point of $V\cap W$ has a neighbourhood, open in the subspace $V\cap W$, on which $g$ is constant). Put $a=g(y)$ and let $w\in V\cap W$. There is an open $O\subseteq Y$ with $w\in O\cap V\cap W$ such that $g$ is constant on $O\cap V\cap W$ (subspace-open sets of $V\cap W$ have the form $O\cap V\cap W$, $O$ open in $Y$). The set $O\cap V$ is open in $Y$ and meets $W$ (in $w$), so $y\in O\cap V$ by Step 1, hence $y\in O\cap V\cap W$ and $g(w)=g(y)=a$. Thus $g$ is the constant map with value $a$.

source.place: Modules, proof of Lemma Tag 0CAL (label lemma-constructible-in-constant, line 3133), the omitted claim 'i_{x,*}F_x is a constant sheaf on the closure of x'; written out by the agent

proof.text: *Step 3 (each $\kappa_V$ is well defined and bijective).* Let $V\subseteq Y$ be open. Case $y\in V$: $(i_{y,*}A)(V)=A$, and for $a\in A$ the constant map $c_a:V\cap W\to A$ with value $a$ is locally constant, so $\kappa_V(a)=c_a\in(i_W)_*\underline A_W(V)$. It is injective because $V\cap W\ni y$ is nonempty, so $c_a(y)=a$ recovers $a$; it is surjective because by Step 2 every locally constant $g:V\cap W\to A$ equals $c_{g(y)}$. Case $y\notin V$: by Step 1 $V\cap W=\emptyset$, so $(i_W)_*\underline A_W(V)$ consists of exactly one element, the empty map (which is locally constant), and $(i_{y,*}A)(V)=\{*\}$; the map $\kappa_V:*\mapsto\emptyset$ between one-point sets is bijective.

source.place: Modules, proof of Lemma Tag 0CAL (label lemma-constructible-in-constant, line 3133), the omitted claim 'i_{x,*}F_x is a constant sheaf on the closure of x'; written out by the agent

proof.text:
*Step 4 (compatibility with restrictions).* Let $V'\subseteq V$ be opens of $Y$; we check $\kappa_{V'}(s|_{V'})=\kappa_V(s)|_{V'\cap W}$ for $s\in(i_{y,*}A)(V)$. The case $y\in V'$, $y
otin V$ cannot occur since $V'\subseteq V$. (a) $y\in V'$ (so $y\in V$): the restriction of $i_{y,*}A$ is the identity of $A$, and the restriction of the constant map $c_a$ on $V\cap W$ to $V'\cap W$ is the constant map $c_a$ on $V'\cap W$; both sides are $c_a$ for $s=a$. (b) $y\in V$, $y
otin V'$: $s|_{V'}=*$ and $\kappa_{V'}(*)$ is the empty map; $V'\cap W=\emptyset$ by Step 1, so $\kappa_V(s)|_{V'\cap W}$ is also the empty map. (c) $y
otin V$ (so $y
otin V'$): $s=*$, $s|_{V'}=*$, and both sides are the empty map on $V'\cap W=\emptyset$. Hence $\kappa=(\kappa_V)_V$ is a morphism of presheaves of sets $i_{y,*}A	o(i_W)_*\underline A_W$.

proof.text: *Step 5 ($\kappa$ is an isomorphism of sheaves of sets).* (a) $(i_W)_*\underline A_W$ is a sheaf: let $V=\bigcup_jV_j$ be an open covering and $g_j:V_j\cap W\to A$ locally constant with $g_j=g_k$ on $V_j\cap V_k\cap W$. The sets $V_j\cap W$ cover $V\cap W$, so there is exactly one map $g:V\cap W\to A$ with $g|_{V_j\cap W}=g_j$ for all $j$; it is locally constant since each point lies in some $V_j\cap W$, which is open in $V\cap W$, and has there a neighbourhood open in $V_j\cap W$ (hence in $V\cap W$) on which $g=g_j$ is constant. (b) By Steps 3 and 4, the maps $\kappa_V^{-1}$ are inverse bijections and commute with restrictions as well (apply $\kappa_{V'}^{-1}$ and $\kappa_V^{-1}$ to the identity of Step 4), so $\kappa$ is an isomorphism of presheaves of sets; in particular $i_{y,*}A$, being isomorphic to the sheaf of (a), is a sheaf of sets (as also follows from Definition 009A: it is the direct image $V\mapsto A(i_y^{-1}V)$ of the sheaf $A$ on the one-point space $\{y\}$, whose value on $\emptyset$ is a one-point set), and $\kappa:i_{y,*}A\to(i_W)_*\underline A_W$ is an isomorphism of sheaves of sets.
